newsitem.title: FINLAND: Active Helsinki lifted by strong Merita, Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Active Helsinki lifted by strong Merita, Nokia.

text.p: Shares closed active trading on Friday sharply higher on strength in banking group Merita Oy and telecom bluechip Nokia Oy, with U.S. payroll figures further bolstering confidence, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 0.94 percent to 2223.60, bringing the index up 2.3 percent for the week. Volume was heavy at 579 million markka.
Merita gained 0.90 markka to close at 11.60 in unusually heavy 76 million markka volume. Brokers said demand was sparked by a Merita road show targetting big U.S. investors.
"Evidently (Merita CEO) Vesa Vainio has been saying good things in America," one broker said. "I don't know what Vainio has been saying, but it seems to have worked," another said.
Nokia rose 6.00 markka to end at 216.00 in what was seen as a spillover of interest generated by Nokia's announcement on Thursday of a big mobile phone deal with telecom giant AT&T.
Adding strength in financial industry shares was insurer Sampo, which rose 7.00 markka to 340.00 in active trading.
Despite the upbeat mood, the market's strength was not particularly broad. Decliners outnumbered advancers, and forestries softed slightly in absence of demand.
Brokers said the new U.S. payroll figures stoked confidence that no U.S. interest rate hike was on the cards. "The figures were lousy enough," one broker said.
Brokers were mixed about Merita's chances for further gains. "We think it's at its upper end," one broker said, while another saw an upside to the stock during the next few weeks.
